On Nov 2, 2008, at 17:47 , Abdel wrote:

> Hi,
> I’m trying to launch RServe.exe directly from a java app, sample  
> code :

That code won't work for several reasons -- 1) you have to supply I/O  
consumers or Java will block the process and 2) R requires you to  
specify the behavior on exit, so at the very least you have to pass  
either --save or --no-save (see R documentation).

Given that this issue pops up more frequently, I have added a class  
StartRserve to the Rserve sources to illustrate how to properly start  
Rserve in a platform-independent manner. The class is now in the  
Rserve sources but also viewable from SVN at
http://svn.rforge.net/org/trunk/rosuda/REngine/Rserve/test/StartRserve.java

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: problems updating rJava
messages.body_plain:
On Oct 28, 2008, at 15:34 , J. garribia wrote:

> Hi, I´m developing a clustering software in java( win xp), and I use  
> rJava to comunicate Java with R. I know that the versions of rJava  
> and R must be compatible for them to work. Can somebody please tell  
> me how to proceed  if I update rJava and R ? Do I need to changed  
> some code in my soft? because  I want to make a friendly  
> installation and  with this requirements it gets cumbersome.
>
>
>

The only requirement is that you re-install rJava after installing new  
R version. That is true for all (binary) R packages, not just rJava.  
However, make sure that you have configured your new R with Java  
support - it is something easily forgotten.

Cheers,
Simon

There is exactly the same question in the archives, but no solution

I created two web processes of which one is an optional successor of  
the other. If the second process is executed, it needs one R-object  
of the first process.

There is a Tomcat machine and a Rserve machine running and for  
different reasons I don't want to save the R-object on the Rserve  
machine but in the webapps directory of the Tomcat. So what is the  
best way to transfer R-objects from Rserve to JRClient and back to  
Rserve?


Christian

messages.body_plain:
On Nov 20, 2008, at 4:31 , System.out.println at web.de wrote:

> can anybody tell me how to transfer R-objects between Rserve and the  
> client?
>

Huh? That's exact what Rserve does. Any call to eval will transfer R- 
object to the client and assign will send an object from the client to  
Rserve.


> There is exactly the same question in the archives, but no  
> solution   had been postet.
>

?


> I created two web processes of which one is an optional successor  
> of  the other. If the second process is executed, it needs one R- 
> object  of the first process.
>
> There is a Tomcat machine and a Rserve machine running and for  
> different reasons I don't want to save the R-object on the Rserve  
> machine but in the webapps directory of the Tomcat. So what is the  
> best way to transfer R-objects from Rserve to JRClient and back to  
> Rserve?
>

[JRclient is the old API that's no longer maintained, I suggest you  
use REngine instead]

That's trivial - retrieve the object on the Java side (eval), store it  
and send it back (assign) in the next Rserve instance. Depending on  
your object and purpose you may want to serialize it before  
transporting (use serialize()/unserialize() in R). You can perform the  
serialization at either end. If the object is simple enough and you  
need to inspect the object on the Java side, use Java serialization,  
otherwise I'd recommend R-side serialization.

Cheers,
S

messages.body_plain:
On Nov 21, 2008, at 8:38 AM, System.out.println at web.de wrote:

> Thanks Simon,
>
> you are right. I was not aware of REXP and thought Rserve can only
> send objects to the client that can be assigned to Java objects, like
> int, double, arrays etc.
>
> But there is still a problem. It's not really an Rserve problem, but
> related to it. Maybe you can give me another hint.
>
> Transfering R-objects is not the problem anymore, as long as I have
> the REXP-object (i.e. do  eval and assign directly one after the
> other). But in my case I have to write this object to a file and
> later have to read it back into Java and subsequently transfer it to
> Rserve. What I do is:
>
> // Get R-object
> REXP testObj = c.eval("R.object");
> byte [] testObjByte = testObj.asBytes();
>
> // Write to file
> File f = new File("path/to/somewhere.dat");
> ObjectOutputStream out = new ObjectOutputStream( new FileOutputStream
> (f) );
> out.writeObject(testObjByte);
> out.close();
>
> // Read back
> ObjectInputStream in = new ObjectInputStream( new  
> FileInputStream(f) );
> Object testObjBack = in.readObject();
> in.close();
>
> Now I've got an Java-Object. But how do I get it back into Rserve?
> There's no possibility to assign a Java-Object to an R-object, right?

You just cast it - that's all:
REXP r = (REXP) in.readObject();

Note, however, that not all types are supported in assigning. If you  
have problems, do the serialization on R side, get the raw bytes from  
the resulting REXP and store that instead. Let me know if you  
encounter any issues.

Cheers,
S

R.

Say I call a Java function which returns a multidimensional array, once the
array has been assigned to a R variable (using .jevalArray). What happens
to the Java objects? Are those garbage collected? Does the R side need to
do anything special to free that memory?

Also when java objects are available in R, do they ever get marked for
garbage collection?

Cheers,

// Giuseppe

messages.subject: Re: rJava & memory management
messages.body_plain:
Giuseppe,

On Nov 24, 2008, at 12:51 , giuseppe1.milicia at hsbcib.com wrote:

> I was wondering if there was any documentation about the memory  
> management of rJava. Google did not bring much up...
>

Well, it's not doing anything special - the regular rules in both  
languages apply, so I don't see what's to document here :). An object  
can only be released when there are no references to it. That's the  
commonly used strategy everywhere and that's all that happens.


> Essentially I was wondering what happens when I move objects from  
> Java to R.
>
> Say I call a Java function which returns a multidimensional array,  
> once the array has been assigned to a R variable  
> (using .jevalArray). What happens to the Java objects?

It becomes a globally referenced object, i.e. it will live for at  
least as long in Java as the reference to it does on the R side. As  
soon as the R reference object is released, it releases that global  
reference in Java.


> Are those garbage collected? Does the R side need to do anything  
> special to free that memory?
>

The R side automatically releases the corresponding Java object once  
the reference object on the R side is released (garbage-collected).  
There is nothing special to do here.


> Also when java objects are available in R, do they ever get marked  
> for garbage collection?
>

The regular R object rules apply - there is nothing special about Java  
reference objects. Keep in mind that in each language you are dealing  
with a proxy object, so they always behave the same as any other  
object in that language/system.


The only interesting issue here is that both systems use garbage  
collectors. Those rely on (among other things) the tracking of sizes  
of objects to make decisions, so the interplay of both garbage  
collectors can lead to a more heavy memory use, because neither  
collector is aware of the size of the referenced objects. Therefore it  
may be advisable to occasionally force garbage collection (depending  
on the application.) In practice, however, this has never surfaced as  
an issue for me.

BTW: if you want to have a peek at the memory usage, compile rJava  
with the debugging and memory profiling enabled - it's fun to watch  
although quite slow ;).

Cheers,
S
